chapter: Reel 3: defining jazz and the blues
title: Jazz covers too much territory; ragtime
summary: Johnson says jazz is pasted onto too much music and that he got nothing out of ragtime.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: We were talking about blues the last time -- we were talking about jazz and definitions of jazz. And one of the things that you said was that jazz encompasses too much territory, and I'd like to have you tell us a little bit more about what you mean.

Well, just like I said, it covers too much territory -- you can put jazz in too many spots, and it doesn't belong in those places. Jazz should have a special spot of its own. They got to throwing jazz around, and just pasted it on the wall everywhere. Jazz, jazz, jazz.
That's a good way to put it -- pasted it on the wall everywhere.
Let's talk about some definitions of jazz. Just off the top of your head, how would you define jazz?
Well, that's be very difficult, identifying jazz, because see, like I said, they play it too many different ways -- too many categories they play jazz in.
Well, let's talk about -- let me
go back to ragtime. They say that that was one of the beginnings of jazz ... do you think so?
Well, to tell you the truth, I came through that era, that period, but I never got anything out of it.
I never was in it, and so not being in it, I got nothing out of it.
